triage_context.environment: Internet-facing web service (HTTP is untrusted). Live-run reachability evidence folded into verify_verdict where it changes the picture.

findings.title: SQL injection in issue search
findings.rationale: `q` is concatenated into CommandText (IssueRepository.cs:20-21), reached unauth from Program.cs:25. No parameterization. Confirmed exploitable live: `' OR 1=1--` returned all rows; UNION extracted sqlite_version(). 0 preconditions, unauth → HIGH.
findings.owner_hint: component: Data/; no CODEOWNERS; single committer

findings.title: OS command injection in report export
preconditions: send a POST /reports/export with a crafted label (no auth)
findings.rationale: `label`/`format` concatenated into a /bin/sh -c string (ReportExporter.cs:13), reached unauth from Program.cs:32. Confirmed exploitable live: injected `id` ran as the service account and its output returned in the HTTP response; a file was written to /tmp. 0 preconditions, unauth → HIGH.
findings.owner_hint: component: Export/; no CODEOWNERS; single committer

findings.title: Insecure deserialization (TypeNameHandling.All)
preconditions: the request body is read asynchronously (AllowSynchronousIO=true) OR Restore() is invoked from a non-HTTP path
a usable gadget type is loadable in the process
findings.rationale: SerializerSettings use TypeNameHandling.All (BackupService.cs:10), honoring attacker $type — sink CONFIRMED by direct invocation of the compiled method (instantiated System.Text.StringBuilder from the wire, reached for EvilAssembly). BUT over HTTP the endpoint throws first: reader.ReadToEnd() is a synchronous body read, blocked by ASP.NET's default AllowSynchronousIO=false (verified live: every body → 500 before the deserializer). Real sink, gated HTTP path → severity downgraded from HIGH to MEDIUM, verify_verdict needs_manual_test.
findings.owner_hint: component: Restore/; no CODEOWNERS; single committer

findings.title: Path traversal / absolute-path override in attachment read
preconditions: a reverse proxy decodes %2f before ASP.NET, OR Read() is called with a name from a non-HTTP source
findings.rationale: Path.Combine(_storageRoot, name) + File.ReadAllBytes with no containment (AttachmentService.cs:12-13), reached unauth from Program.cs:28. Sink CONFIRMED reachable with raw input (live: handler opened '/var/issueblot/attachments/..%2f...'), but default Kestrel keeps %2f literal for a single-segment {name} route and normalizes real '..' before routing, so the documented HTTP trigger never lands a real '/'. Real code flaw, HTTP trigger neutralized → HIGH downgraded to MEDIUM, needs_manual_test.
findings.owner_hint: component: Files/; no CODEOWNERS; single committer

findings.title: Weak password hashing (unsalted MD5)
preconditions: attacker obtains a stored password hash (e.g. via the SQLi or a DB leak)
findings.rationale: Hash() uses MD5 with only a static pepper and no per-user salt (PasswordHasher.cs:13-14). Confirmed live: the server hash for 'hunter2' matched MD5('hunter2'+pepper) recomputed offline. Fast, unsalted → cheap brute-force once a hash leaks. Kept DISTINCT from f006 (different root cause).
findings.owner_hint: component: Auth/; no CODEOWNERS; single committer

findings.title: Hardcoded pepper in source
preconditions: attacker reads the source or decompiles the assembly (public repo, or via another finding)
findings.rationale: `const Pepper = "s3cr3t-pepper-v1"` is compiled in (PasswordHasher.cs:9) and mixed into every hash (line 14). A secret in source is known to anyone with read access and cannot be rotated, so it adds no entropy — confirmed live by reproducing the server hash with the source value. DISTINCT from f005: fixing MD5 does not remove the hardcoded secret.
findings.owner_hint: component: Auth/; no CODEOWNERS; single committer

findings.title: No authentication on any endpoint
findings.rationale: Real observation, but not a discrete actionable defect on its own: it is a missing-hardening/best-practice gap (exclusion rule 13) with no standalone exploit, and the target's THREAT_MODEL explicitly scopes authentication out. It amplifies f001-f006 rather than being independently exploitable. Dropped under precision policy; recorded as a design gap in the threat model (T6) instead.
